newsitem.title: UK: UK's Channel 5 says launch date not yet fixed.
newsitem.headline: UK's Channel 5 says launch date not yet fixed.

text.p: Britain's fifth terrestrial television channel said on Friday it had not yet agreed a launch date with television regulators following its decision last month to postpone its planned January 1 debut.
Channel 5 spokeswoman Sally Osman said that chief executive David Elstein would write to the Independent Television Commission (ITC) next week to suggest a new launch date.
Elstein is waiting for more data on Channel 5's retuning programme before he gets in touch with the watchdog body.
Industry sources said the delay was likely to exceed the 4-6 weeks indicated by Channel 5 when it announced the postponement.

A report in Friday's London Evening Standard said that Channel 5 would not begin broadcasting until the end of March, choosing the Easter period when viewing figures are low and early glitches could pass almost unnoticed.
Channel 5's Osman said the March 26 launch date mentioned in the Standard was guesswork on the part of the newspaper.
Channel 5 blamed the delay on the granting of access last month to a new frequency which will make the channel available in an extra 1.8 million homes -- boosting coverage to 80 percent of the UK.

The decision created more work for Channel 5's engineers who are visiting some 10 million households nationwide to retune video recorders in order to prevent interference from the new channel's signal.
The retuning programme must be 90 percent complete before the station can launch.
Channel 5 Broadcasting is a consortium comprising British media companies Pearson and United News & Media plus Luxembourg broadcast group CLT and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.
